topPRs.title: Add super permissioned dispute game support
topPRs.author: stevennevins
topPRs.body:
Adds the super permissioned dispute game implementation and wires game type 5 through contracts, deployment, proposer, dispute monitor, challenger, and migration validation paths.

The challenger now registers a dedicated super-permissioned actor that compares proposed super roots against supervisor/supernode data, challenges invalid games, and resolves valid games after the challenge window.

This also updates game argument encoding, deployment/manage flags, ABI/storage snapshots, and tests for the new simplified permissioned super-root flow.

Validated with `go test ./op-challenger/game/fault/contracts ./op-challenger/game/fault ./op-dispute-mon/mon/extract ./op-proposer/contracts ./op-chain-ops/interopgen ./op-deployer/pkg/deployer/manage`, `go test ./op-challenger/cmd ./op-challenger/config ./op-challenger/game/fault/contracts ./op-challenger/game/fault`, `forge test --match-contract SuperPermissionedDisputeGame --match-path 'test/dispute/SuperPermissionedDisputeGame.t.sol'`, and `DEV_FEATURE__OPTIMISM_PORTAL_INTEROP=true DEV_FEATURE__SUPER_ROOT_GAMES_MIGRATION=true forge test --match-contract 'OPContractsManagerV2_Migrate_Test|OPContractsManagerStandardValidator_Super|OPContractsManagerMigrationValidator'`.

topPRs.title: fix(op-supervisor/logs): atomic operations and crash-safe recovery
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Closes ethereum-optimism/optimism-private#539.

Makes every mutating `logs.DB` operation atomic — in-memory `lastEntryContext` and on-disk state always advance together, or neither does. Errors never require app-level close/reopen; the next mutation drains pending cleanup and either succeeds or returns the same typed error indefinitely without corruption.

Mechanism:
- Working-clone pattern: `AddLog` accumulates into a clone with no I/O; `SealBlock` does one Write + fsync + atomic swap. Collapses N+2 syscalls per block to 1 Write + 1 fsync.
- `entrydb` `pendingCleanup` carries an explicit truncate-to target. All rollback/cleanup paths converge on `drainCleanup`. The store's `PrepareForMutation` is the single drain entry point for callers.
- `Rewind`/`Clear` use the same shape: swap committed state first, then truncate + fsync. Pending cleanup makes reads observe the smaller bound even if truncate fails.
- Startup recovery requires `logsSince==0` on the SearchCheckpoint preceding a CanonicalHash (skipping periodic checkpoints). If the file ends exactly at a closing boundary, drop that block — its fsync return cannot be proven; post-boundary entries are proof the prior `SealBlock` returned.

Per-block fsync is required: Linux page cache + device write cache reorder freely across non-FLUSH boundaries on NVMe/EBS/pd-ssd, and ext4 delayed allocation can advance `i_disksize` before data blocks are durable.

Crash-injection tests cover the sync-failure and periodic-checkpoint recovery paths; `TestRecoverOnCreate` subtests updated under the new drop-last-block rule.

Plan: \`plans/2026-05-11-fix-logsdb-atomic-operations-plan.md\` (op-claude).

topPRs.title: [codex] add op-reth runtime cross-unsafe head
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
## Summary
- adds an opt-in, repeatable `--rollup.cross-unsafe-head-source-rpc CHAIN_ID=RPC_URL` flag for op-reth
- exposes `eth_crossUnsafeHead` and `eth_getCrossUnsafeHead` when at least one source RPC mapping is configured
- computes the head on demand from an in-memory safe-to-latest cache
- validates local executing messages by selecting the source RPC from the executing message chain ID, then checking the initiating message exists at the claimed source block/log index via remote `eth_getLogs`, with origin/payload-hash checks and the initiating timestamp not after the executing block timestamp

## Scope
This is intentionally a simplified runtime gate. It does not model dependency graph hazards/cycles or message expiry. It stops at the first block that cannot be validated and returns the latest validated cached head, seeded from the local safe head. Missing source-chain RPC mappings fail closed for blocks that execute messages from that chain.

## Validation
- `/Users/karl/.cargo/bin/cargo check -p reth-optimism-rpc -p reth-optimism-node`
- `/Users/karl/.cargo/bin/cargo test -p reth-optimism-rpc cross_unsafe::tests --lib`
- `/Users/karl/.cargo/bin/cargo test -p reth-optimism-node args::tests::test_parse_cross_unsafe_head_source_rpc_args -- --exact`
- `/Users/karl/.cargo/bin/cargo test -p reth-optimism-node args::tests --lib`

topPRs.title: feat(kona): build reproducible prestates with apko
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Migrates the reproducible Kona fault proof prestate build from the Dockerfile-based flow to a melange/apko-based flow.

- Adds melange package config for building `kona-client` / `kona-client-int` prestates.
- Adds apko config for composing a minimal image containing the generated prestate artifacts.
- Replaces `just build-kona-reproducible-prestate*` Docker invocation with the new apko/melange build script.
- Preserves existing output layout under:
  - `rust/kona/prestate-artifacts-cannon`
  - `rust/kona/prestate-artifacts-cannon-interop`
- Supports `KONA_CUSTOM_CONFIGS_DIR`.
- Updates CircleCI jobs to install pinned `apko` and `melange` release binaries.
- Keeps CircleCI single-variant publishing efficient by building only the requested Kona variant.

## Verification

- Ran default reproducible Kona prestate builds successfully.
- Confirmed generated hashes match existing checked-in artifacts
- Tested prestate builds with custom configs
